auditor: Codex resumed coverage audit conceptual solver
key_exposure: Only the answer-free conceptual packet and preserved numerical solution files were inspected before freezing these conceptual judgments. No current question keys or prior receipt workings were consulted.
selection: Sixteen deliberately stratified conceptual questions; not a random statistical sample.

results.working: Temperature is a state variable. A rate requires a mechanism law and its boundary data: for example Fourier conduction needs conductivity and a gradient, convection needs h and fluid temperature, and radiation needs the radiative environment.
results.alternative_choices_review: Temperature times area lacks power units; absolute high temperature does not establish an outward sign; a steady body can pass heat through it.

results.working: For constant k, the steady one-dimensional balance is k T_xx + q_gen = 0. Positive uniform generation therefore gives nonzero curvature T_xx = -q_gen/k.
results.alternative_choices_review: A nonzero generation term precludes a universally constant gradient; thickness and surface boundary conditions continue to affect the solution; prescribed surface temperatures do not require zero flux.

results.working: Effectiveness follows the coupled stream energy balances and boundary conditions. Parallel and counterflow arrangements have different inlet boundary placement and generally different epsilon(NTU, Cr) functions.
results.alternative_choices_review: NTU alone omits Cr and configuration; Cr still matters in counterflow; equality at special limiting conditions does not make effectiveness universally identical.

results.working: The mean coefficient for a constant-width plate is (1/L) integral_0^L h(x) dx, whereas h_L samples a single position. The mean requires the distribution.
results.alternative_choices_review: A varying positive h does not average to zero, and an endpoint alone does not determine an integral.
results.qualification: Read the answer as distinguishing the quantities and their definitions: specially constructed nonmonotone distributions can have mean equal to the endpoint despite variation, so literal universal numerical inequality is too strong.

results.working: If T solves the compatible constant-k pure-Neumann problem, T+C has exactly the same gradient and boundary flux for any constant C. A point temperature or prescribed mean fixes this constant.
results.alternative_choices_review: Neither zero flux nor k fixes an absolute Celsius reference; the stated global compatibility condition addresses existence rather than uniqueness of the temperature offset.

results.working: Energy conservation uses divergence of Fourier heat flux: div(k(T) grad T). Expanding it produces k Laplacian(T) + (dk/dT)|grad T|^2, so k cannot generally be moved outside the divergence.
results.alternative_choices_review: Conservation still applies, and conduction flux remains linked to the temperature gradient. Laplacian(T)=0 alone drops the conductivity derivative.

results.working: Linearize about P=A q(T0): C d(deltaT)/dt=-A q_prime(T0) deltaT. For positive physical area and C with q_prime<0, the perturbation grows: an increase in T lowers heat removal.
results.alternative_choices_review: P is explicitly fixed, C stays positive, and the negative slope means removal decreases rather than increases.

results.working: x_eq<0 means h<h_f at the local pressure, on the subcooled-liquid side of the equilibrium saturation interval. It is an enthalpy coordinate outside [0,1], not a negative physical vapor mass fraction.
results.alternative_choices_review: Neither negative vapor flow nor negative area follows; the superheated-vapor side would have x_eq>1.

results.working: Additional radiation changes heat delivery to the liquid interface and evaporation; these can change vapor-film thickness and the conductive film coefficient. Applicability of simple addition must be checked against a coupled model and its boundary conditions.
results.alternative_choices_review: Distinct mechanisms can still interact through the state; a vapor film does not force radiation to zero; a gray-surface evaluation does not supply all film boundary conditions.

results.working: An opposing interfacial shear contributes with sign to the momentum balance. In a local planar-film solution its contribution to the drainage rate is rho_l tau_i delta^2/(2 mu_l); upward tau_i opposes gravity drainage and can alter thickness or invalidate the assumed regime.
results.alternative_choices_review: The effect depends on shear direction; small film Reynolds number does not imply zero interface shear; external plates and internal condensation have different geometrical and dynamical conditions.

results.working: Total heat rate depends on the population integral of individual-drop transfer, covered area, nucleation and departure. Equality of one mean diameter does not determine these nonlinear contributions.
results.alternative_choices_review: Equal mean size cannot eliminate dynamics, force identical heat-transfer coefficients, or remove conduction resistance through drops.

results.working: At steady temperature, external absorption and emission can have a nonzero difference balanced by active cooling. Zero storage is an overall steady energy balance, whereas radiative thermal equilibrium requires the appropriate radiative detailed balance.
results.alternative_choices_review: Steadiness does not set all rates to zero or alter material properties to unity, and it does not require matching absorption and emission at each wavelength.

results.working: Fixed-frame stagnancy of B imposes N_B=0, and N_A is nonzero. Thus N_total=N_A, and N_A=J_A+y_A N_A includes the molar-average convective contribution (Stefan flow).
results.alternative_choices_review: Equimolar counterdiffusion would require N_B=-N_A; setting N_A or J_A to zero contradicts or unnecessarily restricts the supplied situation.

results.working: Under the thin-film, negligible inertia and negligible interface-shear approximation, integrating the local balance mu u_yy=-(rho_l-rho_v) g_t gives a parabolic velocity profile. Integrating velocity over film thickness yields Gamma=rho_l(rho_l-rho_v) g_t delta^3/(3 mu_l); geometry enters the tangential gravity and local film thickness.
results.alternative_choices_review: Film thickness is not universal; constant gravitational magnitude does not imply constant tangential driving; the linear temperature assumption does not itself determine momentum integration.
results.qualification: The displayed g must mean the local tangential gravity component. If interpreted as the constant magnitude, the claim of validity at every point on a cylinder or sphere is false. The selected option explicitly supplies g(x), so its intended interpretation is recoverable.

results.working: In the Kandlikar branch structure the horizontal-flow factor modifies the convection-dominated Co contribution. The nucleate-boiling Boi contribution retains its own fluid/surface factor F. Thus the branch is R[a Co^m f_o + b Boi^n F].
results.alternative_choices_review: Putting f_o on the nucleate term, taking its reciprocal, or applying it to both terms changes the specified physical branch dependence.

results.working: Ra_D=2e10 exceeds the stated upper applicability limit 1e9 by a factor of 20. The finite algebraic value is not evidence of validity; an applicable regime and geometry correlation is needed.
results.alternative_choices_review: Finiteness does not justify extrapolation; a sphere has different geometry; replacing length by area is dimensionally invalid.
